when: their top or mid laner is level 6 and yours is level 5, between 5:00 and 8:00
asks: can I fight for this crab
their top just hit six, do I still go crab
crab's up, their laner's walking down
say: Give this crab and take your camps toward the other side, or contest only if your own laner can walk over first.
more: A solo laner who hits six first can leave lane and stand in the river with an ultimate. That turns a jungle duel into a fight you start a player and a spell down.
The crab matters most as experience toward your own six. Camps on the other side give you the same thing without the coin flip.
A minute later the levels even out and the next river fight is on equal terms, as long as you didn't die for this one.
check: Is their six-level laner actually leaving lane, and is your laner's wave pushed enough to follow?
breaks: Wrong if their laner is stuck under his own tower with a big wave: then the river is a straight duel and you can take it.
basis: pro:A laner's level six owns the river

when: you are level 5
asks: I'm almost six, gank or farm
should I gank now or wait for ult
one camp off six, what do I do
do I finish my camps first
when do I start using Paranoia
say: Finish the one or two camps to six, then Paranoia a lane with no Flash, or gank now only if a lane's already winning.
more: Paranoia cuts their vision and lets you launch at a champion, so your ganks stop depending on walking past wards. A walk-up gank a camp earlier is a much weaker version of the same play.
Getting six before their jungler gives you a short stretch where you can start a play he can't answer in kind.
Pick the lane by who can't escape. A target with his own safety ultimate or Flash up often just walks away from it.
check: Which enemy laners have used Flash, and is the lane you want close enough to reach with the ult?
breaks: Wrong if a lane is about to be dived right now: go help with what you have, the level can wait a camp.
basis: pro:Finish the level before the ult gank

asks: both my carries burned flash, where do I go
my bot has no flash, do I stay near
should I cover bot or keep farming
say: Clear toward the lane with no Flash and sit behind it while the wave pushes in, or farm away if their jungler shows elsewhere.
more: A carry with no Flash is the easiest target on the map, and their jungler knows it. Standing behind that lane turns his gank into your counter-gank.
You only need to be there while the wave is walking toward their tower. Once it crashes and your laner backs off, go back to camps.
It costs you a little farm now and saves a kill that would have fed the gank after it too.
check: Which of your laners actually has Flash down, and where was their jungler last seen?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler just showed on the far side: take your camps or gank the lane he left instead of waiting for nothing.
basis: pro:Babysit the lane with no Flash

when: you have Teleport and a fight is starting at an objective
asks: I'm about to take this tower, do I leave
they're fighting at herald, do I tp
say: Finish the tower first, then Teleport in if it's nearly dead, or leave it now if your team is already fighting outnumbered.
more: A tower that needs a few more hits is guaranteed gold, and Teleport still gets you to the fight. You get paid on both sides of the map.
The risk is the seconds your team plays a player down. If they can back off and reset the objective while you finish, it's free.
Arriving a little late but behind the enemy is often a better angle than walking in with everyone.
check: How much health does the tower have, is your Teleport up, and has the fight already started?
breaks: Wrong if the tower is still healthy or your team is already losing people: leave it and go, or don't go at all and keep pushing.
basis: pro:Take the tower, then Teleport to the fight

when: an objective is up or a fight is starting on one side
asks: they're fighting top, do I go
should I roam or stay mid
can I leave lane for herald
their mid's still here, do I move
say: Shove the wave into their tower before you move, so their mid loses minions to follow, or stay and take plates if they leave first.
more: If you clear waves faster, every wave you push pins their mid laner under his tower. He either stays and his team is a player short, or he follows and pays for it in farm.
That also holds his Teleport: using it to join means the next wave dies to the tower with nobody there.
If he walks away before you do, don't race him. Plates and a pushed mid wave are a fair answer.
check: Is your wave already past the middle, and is their mid laner still in lane?
breaks: Wrong if the fight has already started right next to you: go now, the wave isn't worth losing a four against five.
basis: pro:Wave clear holds their mid in lane

when: after 20:00, your team is hitting Baron and their jungler is alive
asks: they're coming, do we finish baron
their jungler's right there, what now
say: Stop hitting it before it gets low and turn on them, or finish it only if their jungler's been pushed out of range.
more: A low Baron with their jungler nearby is a coin flip on Smite. Pulling off early keeps it at a health where a steal isn't possible yet.
You are the healthier side only if you stop early; Baron keeps hurting whoever stands on it.
Win the fight or chase them off first, and the Baron is still sitting there afterward with nobody to contest it.
check: How low is Baron, where is their jungler standing, and how healthy is your front line?
breaks: Wrong if they are too far to arrive before it dies: finish it instead of dropping a free Baron.
basis: pro:Pull off Baron before it can be stolen

asks: I got his flash but no kill, go again
he flashed to tower, do I dive
do I come back to this lane
he got away with flash, now what
say: Count the burned Flash as the win and come back after your next clear, or dive now only with a big wave under his tower.
more: A laner who reaches his tower is usually safe for now. Following him in without a wave to take the tower shots gives the kill back.
The Flash is gone for a few minutes, so the same gank after one more clear has a much better chance of finishing.
Tell your laner. He can stand further up and trade harder while that Flash is down, which sets up the return visit.
check: Did he really use Flash, how many minions are heading to his tower, and where is his jungler?
breaks: Wrong if he keeps getting to tower even without Flash: that lane is too safe, so spend the time on another lane or your camps.
basis: pro:A forced Flash is a return ticket

when: your team has more dragons than theirs and fewer kills
asks: we're behind but we have dragons, what's the plan
we're losing fights but have drakes
do we keep going for dragon
they're up in gold, what do we do
say: Keep trading for dragons and don't take even fights; soul is your way back, or give one if you'd have to fight outnumbered.
more: Gold leads shrink as items finish, but dragon stacks stay. An early soul can outweigh a gold lead that looked large on paper.
Each dragon you take also forces them to come to you at the next one, which is the fight you want: on your terms, at a set time.
Recalls and Teleports should be planned around the dragon timer, not around side waves.
check: How many dragons does each team have, and when does the next one spawn?
breaks: Wrong if they are the ones one dragon from soul: then you can't keep giving, and the next dragon is the fight to plan for.
basis: pro:Dragons carry a team that is behind in gold

when: after 14:00, mid outer towers are still standing
asks: do I go side lane or stay mid
should I group or farm mid
say: Hold mid yourself and send your marksman to a side wave, or group if they bring four or five to your tower.
more: A mage who clears a wave in one rotation makes the mid lane a wall. Nothing gets through, so the mid tower stays up without help.
That frees a teammate to pick up a side wave instead of everyone sharing one lane's gold.
Mid is also the shortest walk to both pits, so you are the first one to the next objective.
check: Can you clear a full wave before it reaches your tower, and how many enemies are showing mid?
breaks: Wrong if you need a long time per wave or they dive you under tower: then stay with your team and let a safer clearer hold it.
basis: pro:A wave-clear mage parks mid

when: after 20:00, your team is partway through Baron or elder dragon
asks: they're coming to contest, what do I do
do I stay on baron or go at them
team's on the objective, where do I stand
say: Walk at them and make them deal with you while the team finishes, or stay and tank the pit if you'd die before it's done.
more: One tanky body in their path buys the seconds the objective needs. They either burn spells on you or walk around and arrive late.
It can cost your life. A death for Baron or elder is a good price; a death and no objective is the worst result, so only go when it's close to done.
If you have a way out, keep it for after the objective falls.
check: How much health is left on the objective, and how many of them are coming through one path?
breaks: Wrong if the objective is still healthy: you die long before it falls, so pull everyone off and fight together instead.
basis: pro:One body buys the objective

when: between 5:00 and 7:00
asks: should I fight him at second crab
can I beat him at scuttle
he's stronger than me, do I go crab
how do I win the crab fight
say: Get to the next crab early and wait in the river brush, or skip it if their jungler has the level lead and help nearby.
more: Arriving first lets you start the fight from a brush with a charged or aimed ability landing before he sees you. That opening can flip a duel you'd lose face to face.
After both first crabs die only one comes back, so it's contested and worth being early for. Remember it can't be up before about 5:25.
If he doesn't come, you take the crab untouched and keep moving.
check: Which side did the crab spawn on, are both first crabs dead, and which of your lanes can move?
breaks: Wrong if their mid and side lane are pushed in on yours: a brush doesn't beat three people, so take camps instead.
basis: pro:First to the brush wins the crab

when: you just reached level 6
asks: do I help push the wave
where do I gank with my ult
does it matter if they see me
say: Stay off the mid wave and out of sight until your ult gank, or show mid on purpose if you're actually going the other way.
more: Every time you show, they know which camps you'll clear next and which lane is safe for the next half minute.
A first ultimate works best when nobody is sure you have it. Keep it hidden until the lane you want is pushed up.
Showing can also be a tool: appear on one side, then cross through your own jungle while they relax on the other.
check: Did a ward or a wave just reveal you, and which lane is pushed far enough to gank?
breaks: Wrong if your mid is about to lose a tower plate or die: show up and help, the surprise isn't worth a lost lane.
basis: pro:Showing gives away the next thirty seconds

when: you are melee against a magic damage laner, on your first or second recall
asks: what do I buy against this mage
he keeps poking me, what do I build
first back, what do I get
I can't walk up to the wave
say: Buy magic resist with some regen first so you can stand in the wave, or buy damage if you're already ahead on kills.
more: A melee champion loses these lanes by being poked off the minions. An early resist component lets you take the hits and keep farming.
It delays your damage item a little, but you arrive at the mid game even in farm instead of a wave or two behind.
Once you can stand in the wave, their jungler has a harder time too, because you're no longer low when he arrives.
check: How much gold do you have, and how much of his damage is coming from abilities?
breaks: Wrong if you already have a kill lead and can force all-ins: damage ends the lane faster than resistance does.
basis: pro:Resist first when melee into a mage

when: you have Teleport, a dragon is up and your far tower is under attack
asks: do I tp top to save the tower
tower's getting hit, we're at dragon
should I leave for the tower
catch bot wave or tp top
say: Catch the wave near the dragon and let the far tower take damage, or Teleport only if the tower's about to fall and dragon's secure.
more: Staying on the near wave keeps you one walk from the pit. Teleporting away removes you from the dragon and leaves that wave to die at your tower.
A damaged tower is still a tower. A lost dragon is one step closer to their soul or one further from yours.
If the dragon is already won, the Teleport is free to use on the tower afterward.
check: How low is the far tower, where is the nearest wave, and has the dragon fight been decided?
breaks: Wrong if the dragon doesn't matter to either team's soul race and the tower is the first one of the game: save the tower.
basis: pro:Catch the wave beside the objective

when: one or more of their carries has a stasis or revive item
asks: I can't kill their carry anymore
how do I find a pick now
say: Pick the target with no stasis or revive item, or bait the item out and go back in when your team follows.
more: Those items turn your full combo into a pause, and your team's follow-up arrives after you've already used everything.
The carry without one, or the support, is often the real opening. A kill there still makes the fight uneven.
If the protected carry is the only target, go in once to force the item, get out, and treat the second entry as the real one.
check: Which of their champions has finished a stasis or revive item, and has it been used recently?
breaks: Wrong if your team has enough follow-up to kill through it: then go on the carry and let the others finish after the item.
basis: pro:Picks fail into stasis and revive

when: before 6:00
asks: is it ok to roam now
wave's pushed, where do I go
say: Roam to mid or river after you shove the wave, and leave once a Flash is burned, or stay if your marksman can't hold alone.
more: A short roam that forces one Flash is worth more than a long one that hunts for a kill. You're back in lane before your marksman loses much.
Push first. With the wave under their tower your marksman is safe, and their support has to choose between following you and the minions.
A burned Flash mid sets up your jungler's next visit there a couple of minutes later.
check: Is your wave pushed all the way in, and can their duo all-in your marksman while you're gone?
breaks: Wrong if their lane has kill pressure on your marksman or the wave is coming toward you: stay, the roam costs a death and a wave.
basis: pro:A short roam for one Flash

when: their jungler's item list just changed
asks: he just backed, where's he going
say: He's back at the camps he took first, so the lane beside those plays safe, or the far lane can step up for a bit.
more: Camps come back in the order they were killed, roughly two minutes and a quarter later. After a recall, a jungler restarts where his clear began.
That makes the lane beside his first camps the next one in danger, and the opposite lane the one with a little room.
It's a guess that gets better with a ward on one of his camps.
check: Which side did he start his clear on, and has anyone seen him since he bought?
breaks: Wrong if he recalled after a kill or a gank instead of a clear: his camps may all be up, so treat him as anywhere.
basis: pro:After a recall he restarts at his first camps

when: their top laner's items just changed and a dragon is up
asks: their top just backed, is dragon free
do we wait for our adc
is this a good time for dragon
say: Start dragon now while their top laner is in base, even without your marksman, or wait if their mid has the wave pushed.
more: A top laner who just bought is the furthest player from the bottom river. It's slower without your marksman, but nobody extra can arrive in time.
The only players who can answer are their mid and jungler, so your mid's wave decides whether it's safe.
An early dragon taken like this costs nothing elsewhere and starts your count toward soul.
check: Does their top laner have Teleport ready, and is your mid wave pushed or even?
breaks: Wrong if their top has Teleport up and their bot lane is healthy: he arrives anyway, so set up vision first or take it later.
basis: pro:Dragon while their top is in base

when: your team just started a dragon
asks: we're doing drake, where do I go
say: If the team doesn't need you to finish it, recall and head to your weak side lane, or stay if they're walking in to contest.
more: When you take a dragon, the usual answer is a dive on your far lane. A support who resets early can be standing there when it arrives.
You also come back with wards for the next objective instead of leaving the dragon with an empty inventory.
It only works if the dragon is safe without you, so leave when it's clear nobody is coming.
check: Is anyone on their team walking toward the dragon, and is your far lane pushed up or under tower?
breaks: Wrong if their team shows up at the pit: your body and spells matter more there than on the other side of the map.
basis: pro:Reset during the dragon to cover the trade

when: your marksman is dead or in base
asks: adc's gone, what do I do
where do I stand while adc is back
can I set up something mid
say: Stand in the brush beside mid while their mid laner is pushed up, or go back bot when your marksman returns.
more: A support nobody sees near mid makes their mid laner's position a risk. If he stays too long, you and your jungler have a dive.
Even without a play, your mid gets room to push and take plates while their mid backs off from the threat.
Leave on time. A wave lost bot because you were late back costs your marksman more than the pressure gained.
check: Is their mid laner past the middle of the lane, and where is your jungler?
breaks: Wrong if a big wave is about to crash into your empty bot tower: hold that wave for your marksman instead.
basis: pro:Hover mid while your marksman is away

asks: I have no flash, can I still push
how do I play with no flash
is it safe to walk up
say: Farm from your side of the wave and let him push until Flash is back, or trade only when your jungler is next to you.
more: An immobile mage with no Flash dies to one gank from either side. The pressure you normally have in this lane isn't worth that for a few minutes.
Giving up the push costs some control of the river, not farm, as long as you last-hit near your tower.
Their jungler will come for you. If yours is waiting, the gank they expected becomes your kill.
check: How long ago did you use Flash, and has their jungler been seen recently?
breaks: Wrong if their mid laner also has no Flash and their jungler just showed far away: then you can keep trading for that moment.
basis: pro:No Flash, no lane pressure

when: an objective spawns within a minute
asks: I have no flash for this fight
should I go to herald with no flash
how do I play this fight flashless
say: With no Flash, stay a screen behind your front line, or take a side wave and let the team give it if they have hard engage.
more: A carry without Flash is the target their engage is looking for. If they reach you, the fight is over before the objective matters.
Standing far back keeps your damage in the fight late rather than not at all.
Against a team full of engage, skipping one early objective and farming a side wave is cheaper than losing the carry and the objective together.
check: Do they have champions who can reach you from range, and is the objective one your team can afford to give?
breaks: Wrong if this objective gives them soul point or Baron: go, stand back, and have your team guard you instead of skipping it.
basis: pro:A carry without Flash changes the objective call

when: before 20:00, their marksman's items just changed and Herald is up
asks: their adc just bought, do we contest
say: Give the dragon and take Herald for a tower, since their marksman just bought, or contest if this dragon puts them on soul point.
more: A marksman fresh from the shop with a new item is at his strongest for that fight. Meeting him at the pit is the worst time to do it.
The top-side objectives turn into tower gold quickly, which is what a team needs when it's slightly behind.
Dragons only pay off as they stack. One given early is recoverable; a lost fight at it usually isn't.
check: How many dragons do they already have, and can your team get to the top pit before they finish?
breaks: Wrong if it is their third dragon or Herald is already gone: then group and contest, or trade for towers.
basis: pro:Herald for a dragon when their carry just bought

when: they have one marksman and no other sustained damage
asks: what do I do in the teamfight
say: Go straight for the one champion who can shred you, or peel your own carry if you can't reach theirs.
more: When only one of them deals steady damage to tanks, removing that player makes your front line very hard to kill for the rest of the fight.
Two of you on the same target is better than one each on different ones. Call who you're going on before it starts.
If their carry is too far back, the fight is won on your side instead, by keeping their divers off your damage.
check: Where is their marksman standing, does he have Flash, and who else on your team can follow you in?
breaks: Wrong if they have a second damage threat, like a fed mage: don't leave your carries alone to chase one player.
basis: pro:Kill the only one who can kill tanks

asks: they're diving me, do I flash
I'm dead, do I use flash
when do I flash a dive
say: If you're dying either way, keep Flash for next time; or Flash late, once they're under the tower, if it gets you out alive.
more: A Flash that doesn't save you is two losses: the death now, and an easier kill on you in a few minutes.
Waiting until they have committed under the tower makes them take more shots while they chase. That's often how a dive becomes a one-for-one.
Decide before they arrive. The worst version is the panic Flash into a wall after the damage is already done.
check: How many are diving, how many minions are under the tower, and can Flash actually get you out of range?
breaks: Wrong if an early Flash reaches a teammate or the next tower cleanly: then use it at once and don't wait.
basis: pro:Hold the Flash that would not save you

asks: how do I know when his camps are up
how do I time his raptors
where do I ward for invades
say: Ward one of his camps, note when he clears it, and come back as it respawns, or just take it if he's shown far away.
more: Small camps return about two minutes and a quarter after they die. One ward that sees the kill tells you exactly when to be back.
A jungler with an odd early path keeps that timing for the whole early game, so the same camp is there for you again and again.
Bring your support or a pushed lane if you can. Arriving on time is no use if he arrives too with help.
check: When did the camp die, and which of your lanes near it has the wave pushed?
breaks: Wrong if the lanes beside that camp are losing: they arrive first, so use the timer to know where he is and gank the other side.
basis: pro:A ward on his camp is a timer

when: their mid is Ryze, Galio or Twisted Fate and is at least level 6
asks: their mid's missing, am I ok
mid's gone, what do I do
say: When their mid goes missing, back off to your tower until he shows, or keep pushing only with a ward behind you and Flash up.
more: Those champions have ultimates that bring them, or their team, to a fight faster than your team can walk. A missing mid can mean a dive is already on its way.
They may send many players for one kill. If you simply aren't there, they've spent time and an ultimate for nothing.
Losing a few minions near your tower is the cheap outcome here.
check: Is their mid visible anywhere, has he used his ultimate recently, and where is their jungler?
breaks: Wrong if his ultimate was just used elsewhere: then the missing mid is only walking, and you have time to finish the wave.
basis: pro:A missing mid with a travel ultimate

when: your team has three dragons and a dragon is up or spawns within a minute
asks: they're going baron side, do we follow
should we split for the other objective
say: Go to the dragon and let them have the other side; soul's worth more, or stall it if you're a player down.
more: Soul is a permanent advantage for the rest of the game. Almost nothing they can take on the other side at the same time matches it.
Teams offer a trade at exactly this moment to pull you away. Sending people across the map is how the soul fight gets lost.
If someone is dead, push waves and delay rather than give up the idea; the dragon will still be there.
check: Is the dragon up now, is your jungler alive with Smite, and how many of them are on the other side?
breaks: Wrong if Baron is what they're taking and you can't finish the dragon before they come back with it: then take soul fast and defend.
basis: pro:Do not trade away soul

when: the enemy started Herald or grubs and your team is not there
asks: they started herald, do we go
say: Don't walk into the pit; cut off whoever is arriving late for them, or take bot plates if nobody's walking up alone.
more: The players already on the objective are grouped. The ones still walking to it are alone, on a known path, and looking at the pit.
A kill on a late arrival can make them drop the objective, or leave them too few to hold it when you turn.
If their whole team is already there, the answer is on the other side of the map instead.
check: Which of their players aren't at the pit yet, and which path would they walk?
breaks: Wrong if all five are already there: there is nobody to catch, so trade for plates or a dragon at once.
basis: pro:Catch the ones walking to the pit

when: you have one more completed item than their marksman
asks: I'm fed, can I just go in
I'm an item up, should I step forward
why did I die when I'm ahead
say: Wait until your front line is next to you before stepping up, or keep poking from range if they're still walking over.
more: An item lead wins fights that last. It doesn't survive being the only target while a teammate is in base or a screen away.
The most common way a fed marksman gives the lead back is starting a fight nobody else was ready for.
Ten seconds of waiting usually changes nothing for them and everything for you.
check: Is anyone on your team in base or dead, and who is close enough to follow you right now?
breaks: Wrong if they are clearly split and one is alone in front of you: then your lead is exactly what kills him before help comes.
basis: pro:A lead needs someone beside it

when: after 20:00, your support is dead and Baron is up
asks: they're on baron, what do we do
say: Clear the waves and hold your towers rather than face-check, or let only your jungler try the steal if it's warded.
more: Without your support you are short on wards and on the spells that keep a walk through the river safe. They know that and start Baron to force you in.
Four walking blind into five is how a lost Baron also becomes a lost base.
Waves cleared now are what lets you defend against the buff afterward.
check: Is there a ward on the pit, how long until your support respawns, and where are the side waves?
breaks: Wrong if you can see they are low or split from a ward: then a quick collapse on the pit can work.
basis: pro:No support, no face-check

when: a few minutes after the enemy took Baron
asks: how do we get vision back
is it safe to leave base
say: Walk out with two teammates and re-ward your own jungle first, or ward the river only if their team shows on the far side.
more: After being held in base, every ward you had is gone and theirs are still there. The first trip out is the one where the support gets caught.
Start close: your jungle entrances, then the river. Each layer makes the next one safer.
A team that picks off the warding support gets the next objective for free, so the escort is worth the lost farm.
check: Where did their team last show, and who can walk with you?
breaks: Wrong if an objective spawns in seconds and they are already on it: skip the slow setup and make the call to give or fight.
basis: pro:Rebuild vision from your own jungle out

when: their mid laner is one component short of a finished item
asks: how do I slow him down
he's about to get his item
he scales harder than me, what do I do
say: Keep the wave on your side so he has to walk up for every minion, or shove and roam if your jungler isn't near.
more: Some champions change completely on their first finished item. Every wave you make hard to collect pushes that moment back.
A wave held near your tower also makes him walk the whole lane to farm, which is where your jungler finds him.
It only works while you can hold it. If he out-pushes you, use the push you do have somewhere else.
check: Can you keep the wave from crashing, and has their jungler shown recently?
breaks: Wrong if an objective is spawning: then push the wave and move, because holding a freeze while your team fights is worse.
basis: pro:Delay the item that changes the champion

when: a dragon spawns within two minutes
asks: dive didn't work, what do we do
we pushed them in, what next
should we keep trying to kill him
say: He got away, so spend the pressure on deep wards around the pit, or recall now if you've got an item to buy.
more: Forcing someone under his tower is still worth something: for a short while nobody can stop you walking into their side of the river.
Wards placed now are still there when the dragon spawns, and they show you who is walking in and from where.
Trying the same dive a second time usually just gives them time to get help.
check: How long until the dragon, how many wards do you have, and is their jungler near?
breaks: Wrong if he is still low under the tower with a big wave coming in: then one more attempt is worth it before you ward.
basis: pro:A failed dive still buys vision

when: your team is behind in kills after 15:00
asks: we're behind, how do we fight
they're fed, what do we do
how do I play teamfights from behind
say: Hold your towers and hit them from range as they walk in, or fall back a tower rather than start a fight yourselves.
more: If your team out-ranges theirs, their lead only counts once they reach you. Each walk forward through your damage costs them health before the fight begins.
A gold lead against a team that scales into longer range shrinks by itself as items finish.
The fight to take is the one where they arrive already hurt, not the one you start.
check: Do they have a way to jump on you from far away, and are Flash and their engage ultimates up?
breaks: Wrong if they are about to take soul or Baron uncontested: range doesn't help if you never show up.
basis: pro:Range makes their gold lead smaller

when: your team won a fight in the last 30 seconds
asks: we won the fight, what now
do we go for the next objective
say: If the big ults are down, buy and start the next objective when they're back, or go right now while three of them are dead.
more: A second fight on empty cooldowns against a team that just respawned is how a won fight gets handed back.
Dead enemies are the exception. With several of them down, an objective needs no ultimates at all.
Spend the gold in between, so the next fight is your new items against their old ones.
check: How many of them are dead and for how long, and which of your key ultimates were used?
breaks: Wrong if nothing is up to take and the waves are pushing into you: fix the waves first, then set up.
basis: pro:Wait for the ultimates before forcing again

when: your marksman is dead or in base
asks: what do I do with the wave
how do I save cs for my adc
say: Hold the wave outside your tower so it waits for your marksman, or let it crash if three of them walk up.
more: A wave that sits in front of your tower is still there when your marksman walks back. One that crashes is gold the tower takes.
Thin it only enough that it doesn't push in. Killing the whole thing sends it away from your marksman.
It also keeps the lane short for them: to stop you they have to walk all the way up.
check: How big is the wave, and are their duo and jungler close enough to dive you?
breaks: Wrong if you are low or they can dive: no wave is worth dying alone, so back off and let the tower have it.
basis: pro:Hold the wave for the one who's away

when: you got a kill and your lane partner died
asks: one for one, do I push
I got the kill, now what
do I stay after the trade
say: Shove the wave only if their support and jungler are still dead or showing elsewhere, or recall right away on that gold.
more: A one-for-one is only good if you also get the wave. That part is where it usually goes wrong.
Their support and jungler often come back onto the map together just as you're pushing alone and low.
Recalling at once still banks the kill gold as an item, which is a real result.
check: Who on their side is alive, how much health do you have, and where was their jungler?
breaks: Wrong if you are healthy and both their bot laners are dead: then push it all the way in and take a plate.
basis: pro:The trade is good only if you keep the wave

asks: how do I not get caught
say: Send Hawkshot into their jungle before you walk past the river, or stay by your tower wall if it's on cooldown.
more: Hawkshot scouts anywhere on the map, so you can check the path a gank would take before you commit to a wave.
When you're ahead, their best way back is catching you alone. Checking first removes that option.
With nothing to scout with, standing where one step gets you to your tower is the same safety by other means.
check: Is Hawkshot available, and which of their players haven't shown?
breaks: Wrong if your team already has wards covering that path: save Hawkshot for the next objective instead.
basis: pro:Scout before you step up

when: you have Teleport, enough gold to finish an item, and an objective spawns within a minute
asks: should I back before the fight
do I buy or go now
I have gold for my item, fight's coming
can I get my item first
say: Recall, finish the item and Teleport to the fight, or walk there now if Teleport's down and you'd arrive late.
more: Showing up with a finished item instead of unspent gold is a real difference in a fight that's about to happen anyway.
Teleport is what makes it free: you lose no time, and you can choose where you arrive.
Tell your team, so they don't start before you're back.
check: Is Teleport ready, and is your team able to wait a few seconds before starting?
breaks: Wrong if the fight has already begun: go as you are, a late item doesn't help a fight that's over.
basis: pro:Finish the item, then Teleport

asks: my mid gank failed, try again
they warded, where do I come from
say: Reset and come back from the other side of mid, where they haven't warded, or go to a side lane if mid's Flash is up.
more: Mid laners usually ward the side they expect you from. After a failed try, the vision is all on that one side.
Recalling and taking the camp or crab on the opposite half puts you on the unwarded entrance without wasting time.
They also relax after seeing you leave, which is when the second angle works.
check: Which side of mid did they ward, and did the first attempt burn any summoner spell?
breaks: Wrong if their mid plays under tower with everything up: neither side works, so put the time into another lane.
basis: pro:Come back from the side they did not ward

when: you are level 5 and a dragon is up
asks: they're doing dragon, do I contest
say: Take the far crab for level six and let the dragon go, or contest it if your lanes get there before theirs.
more: A champion that needs its ultimate to fight is weak at a level 5 dragon. The same minute spent on the far crab makes you a real threat.
They get one early dragon. You get six first on the other side, with a lane right there to use it on.
It's a trade, not a concession, as long as you do something with the level straight away.
check: How close are you to six, is the far crab alive, and which lanes are pushed?
breaks: Wrong if that dragon gives them soul point, or your team is already winning the river: go to the dragon.
basis: pro:Six on the far crab instead of a losing dragon

when: your team is behind after 15:00
asks: how do I find a kill
we can't teamfight, what do I do
should I follow our split pusher
how do I get a pick
say: Walk a step behind your split pusher in the fog and jump whoever comes to stop him, or farm the next wave if two come.
more: A team that plays carefully gives few openings. A split push forces one of them to walk alone to a side lane.
He expects a one against one. Arriving a moment later from the fog turns it into a quick kill, then a tower or an objective.
If they answer with two or more, your team has the numbers everywhere else, so say so.
check: Who is walking to answer the push, and have you been seen on the way?
breaks: Wrong if you were spotted crossing the map: they send more, or start an objective where you aren't.
basis: pro:Shadow the split pusher for a pick

when: after 20:00, the enemy has Baron buff and you are in a side lane
asks: they have baron, do I go back
say: Keep pushing the far lane for a tower while four defend, or go back the moment they commit to an inhibitor.
more: Five defending against Baron usually loses the tower anyway. Four defending while one takes a tower back at least gets paid.
Your push also makes someone leave their siege, which is the only thing that really slows it down.
Watch their group. A real commitment onto an inhibitor is the point where your team needs you there.
check: How many are sieging, can your four clear the empowered waves, and is your Teleport up?
breaks: Wrong if your team can't clear waves without you: an open base costs far more than the tower you take.
basis: pro:Answer a Baron push on the other side

when: two or more enemies have Teleport
asks: should I go for the next tower
why do I keep getting caught splitting
say: Push only to the river unless you see their Teleports used, or go deeper when three of them show on the other side.
more: Every Teleport on their team is another player who can appear behind you in a side lane. Counting who you can see on the map isn't enough.
The far half of the lane is where a collapse works, because the walk back to your tower is too long.
A used Teleport is a short window. That's when the deeper push is actually safe.
check: Which of their Teleports have you seen used recently, and how many of them are visible?
breaks: Wrong if your team is ready to start an objective the moment they send people to you: then pushing deep is the bait working.
basis: pro:Count Teleports before you split

when: before 4:00
asks: can I use everything on camps
is it safe to full clear
say: Keep one dash off the camp while their side lane has the push, or use everything to clear fast if your nearby lanes are winning.
more: When the lane beside you is pushed in, their jungler and that lane can walk into your camp together. With every ability on cooldown, there is no way out.
Holding one escape slows the camp slightly and keeps you alive, which matters far more this early.
When your lanes have the push, nobody can reach you first, so clear as fast as the champion allows.
check: Is the lane next to this camp pushed toward your tower, and has their jungler been seen?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler just showed on the other side of the map: clear at full speed.
basis: pro:Keep an escape while the lane beside you is losing

when: after 20:00, their side laner has more levels and kills than anyone who can face him
asks: nobody can stop their top laner
who goes to the side lane
he's splitting, what do we do
say: Send two to stop him only between objectives, or give that outer tower and group if Baron or dragon is under a minute away.
more: A side laner nobody can duel always costs something. The choice is whether you pay a tower or pay by being short at the pit.
Two players on him right before a spawn is exactly what his team wants.
Between spawns, two can push him back or kill him, and that buys the next objective instead.
check: How long until the next objective, and how far has he pushed?
breaks: Wrong if the tower he is hitting is an inhibitor tower: defend it, even at the cost of the objective.
basis: pro:Pay the tower, not the objective

when: you are behind their jungler in level or gold
asks: I'm behind, how do I come back
their jungler's ahead, what do I do
where do I use my ult
say: Farm to six, then drop Grand Starfall behind a side lane that's pushed up, or hold it for the dragon fight if lanes are even.
more: Grand Starfall puts you into a lane from far away, so it doesn't matter that their jungler wins the duel or owns the river.
Kills in side lanes are how a behind jungler gets gold back without ever meeting the one who's ahead.
Each pick also slows the game down and gives your team room at the next objective.
check: Which enemy lane is pushed far from its tower, and does that laner have Flash?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler is waiting in that lane: landing into a counter-gank from behind makes things worse, so pick another lane.
basis: pro:A cross-map ultimate is the way back

asks: where do I stand in the fight
do I go in or stay back
say: Stand between their divers and your carries at the edge of the fight, or go in on their back line if nobody's diving yours.
more: Holding two of their players out of the fight is worth as much as a kill. Your carries get the seconds they need on everyone else.
It doesn't show on the scoreboard, but a pit fight is often won by the top laner who kept their divers busy on the side.
If they have nobody who dives, that job doesn't exist and your damage belongs on their back line.
check: Which of their champions want to reach your carries, and where are they coming from?
breaks: Wrong if your team has no other way to start the fight: then you are the engage, and the peel falls to the support.
basis: pro:Keep their divers out of the fight

when: before 6:00
asks: we both used flash, what now
no summoners, how do we play
say: Ward the brush behind you, push the wave into their tower and step back, or freeze near yours if you can't get the push.
more: With both Flashes gone, the gank comes from behind, around the long way. A ward there, plus being nowhere near the middle of the lane, takes it away.
Pushing the wave in first means you aren't losing minions while you stand back.
If you can't push, a wave near your own tower does the same job from the other end.
check: Which brush would their jungler come through, and do you have a ward available?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler just showed top: use that moment to play the lane normally.
basis: pro:No Flashes, so ward behind and shove

when: the enemy in your side lane is a tank or a wave-clear mage
asks: he just clears the wave, what do I do
say: Splitting into him won't crack the tower, so shove once and group for the objective, or swap lanes to face someone weaker.
more: A split push works when the defender has to choose between dying and losing the tower. A tank doesn't die, and a mage deletes the wave from range.
Time spent there is time your team plays four against five for nothing.
The lead you built is better used at the next objective, or against whoever is in the other side lane.
check: Can you kill him alone, and does he clear the wave before it reaches the tower?
breaks: Wrong if he has to stay to hold you and your team can take an objective with the numbers: then keep him busy.
basis: pro:A split push needs a defender who can lose

when: you have Teleport and an objective spawns within two minutes
asks: where do I tp for the fight
where do I put a ward for tp
do I walk with the team or tp
how do I use teleport in fights
say: Put a ward behind where they'll stand and Teleport to it once they commit, or walk in with the team if they've swept it.
more: A Teleport behind them closes the exit. A team caught in a choke between your front line and you has nowhere to back off to.
The ward has to go down early, before they clear the area, and somewhere they won't look.
Start it as they commit forward. Too early and they simply turn on you alone.
check: Is the ward still alive, and has their team moved past it toward yours?
breaks: Wrong if your team can't hold for the few seconds the Teleport takes: then you're needed in front from the start.
basis: pro:A flank ward placed before the fight

when: before 6:00
asks: how do I get past the ward
say: Gank bot just after their ward's been used or cleared, through the side they didn't cover, or go elsewhere if it's fresh.
more: Early on each player has one ward on a long timer. Once you know where it went, you know the hole.
Your bot lane can tell you: a ward placed in one brush means the other path is dark for a while.
This is why the strongest early junglers ask about wards before they ask about health bars.
check: Where and when did their bot lane place a ward, and is the wave far enough from their tower?
breaks: Wrong if the wave is under their tower: no ward gap helps when the target is already safe.
basis: pro:Gank through the hole in their wards

when: before level 6
asks: which way do I cross the map
can I gank mid on the way
how do I get to top side
say: Cross through mid lane instead of the river when you change sides; it can force a Flash, or go around if their mid's under tower.
more: Mid is on the way between your two halves. Walking through it costs seconds and gives a free look at a gank.
Even a champion with no early crowd control can force a Flash from an immobile mid laner just by appearing.
A mid laner without Flash has to give up his pressure, and that helps your whole jungle.
check: Is their mid laner past the middle of the lane, and did he ward the side you're coming from?
breaks: Wrong if you're low from your clear or their jungler could be nearby: walk around and keep your camps on time.
basis: pro:Cross the map through mid

when: you are level 6 and even in CS with a ranged mid laner
asks: I'm even with him, is that ok
what do I do at six
how do I play this matchup now
say: Even farm at six means you've won the hard part; look for all-ins when Flash is down, or roam bot with your ult.
more: Ranged mages are supposed to push Akali off the wave early. Reaching six without a deficit means the lane's pressure is gone.
Twilight Shroud makes you hard to punish near your tower, and Perfect Execution gives you two dashes to start or finish a fight.
You don't need the lane kill. An even lane with a free roam is already the result you wanted.
check: Does he have Flash, where is the wave, and is their jungler near mid?
breaks: Wrong if he has both Flash and a stasis item: the all-in fails, so farm and look to side lanes instead.
basis: pro:Even at six is a win for the melee

when: your marksman finished a first item and theirs has not
asks: is this a good time for dragon
my adc has his item, what do we do
say: Force the dragon or a bot fight now, before their item finishes, or take plates if your jungler's on the far side.
more: An early finished item against components is a short edge. It closes the moment their marksman recalls with enough gold.
A team that spikes early has to turn it into something on the map, or the advantage just expires.
Dragon is the natural target: it's beside the lane that holds the lead.
check: How close is their marksman to finishing, and can your jungler get to the bot river?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler and mid are both ahead and nearby: one item doesn't win a fight against three.
basis: pro:Use the first item before theirs arrives

when: an ally died in the last 10 seconds
asks: they killed our support, do we run
we lost one, do we fight
say: They just spent everything on one kill, so turn and fight if you're four healthy, or back off if their carries haven't used anything.
more: A kill that took several ultimates and Flashes leaves them with nothing for the next few seconds.
Losing a support is not the same as losing a carry. If your damage is alive and theirs is on cooldown, four can beat five.
It has to be immediate. A few seconds later the abilities are back and you're just a player down.
check: What did they use to get the kill, who died on your side, and how healthy are your carries?
breaks: Wrong if the one who died was your main damage or they killed him with basic attacks alone: disengage.
basis: pro:Turn on a team that spent everything

when: their team has three or more champions that dive
asks: how do I not get one shot
say: Buy the defensive item first so you survive the dive, or go damage first if you're ahead and their divers are behind.
more: An immobile mage against several divers deals no damage dead. The defensive item is what lets your spells be cast at all.
The price is real: your damage arrives later, and your team has to carry the fights in between.
Say it out loud, so nobody expects you to burst someone during that stretch.
check: How many of their champions can reach you in a fight, and are they ahead or behind?
breaks: Wrong if your team has strong peel and their divers are behind: full damage ends fights before they reach you.
basis: pro:Tanky first into dive, damage later

when: your team is behind and has lost more outer towers
say: Stay five together at the next objective and make them come through you, or defend mid as five if you can't get there first.
more: A team that can't match their side laners loses slowly by spreading out. Every answer to a side wave is a player who can be caught.
Grouped at an objective they need, the map shrinks to one fight, which is the only kind you can win.
You'll lose side towers doing this. That's the price for getting a five against five instead of five small losses.
check: When is the next objective, can you be there first, and how does your team do in a grouped fight?
breaks: Wrong if their team is much better grouped than yours: then clear waves safely and wait for a mistake instead.
basis: pro:Behind and spread out is the worst shape

asks: who goes in the death realm
what do I do in teamfights
say: Take their big engage champion into Realm of Death before he ults, or take their carry if the engage's already been used.
more: Realm of Death removes one player from the fight. Taking the one whose ultimate starts their fight can cancel their whole plan.
It's less flashy than pulling a carry, but against a team built around one big engage it wins more fights.
Once that engage is spent, the best target changes back to whoever deals their damage.
check: Who on their team starts fights, and is that ultimate still available?
breaks: Wrong if their fed carry is the only reason they win fights: then removing or killing him matters more.
basis: pro:Remove the engage, not just the carry

when: you have Teleport and gold for an item component
asks: recall now or one more wave
can I stay for another wave
do I use tp to come back
say: Push this wave in and recall now so you walk back, or stay one more wave only if you're fine spending Teleport.
more: A recall taken late means the next wave arrives at your tower before you do. Then Teleport gets spent just to not lose minions.
That Teleport is the one your team wanted for the first grubs or dragon fight.
Crashing the wave first is what makes the walk back free.
check: Is the wave going to reach their tower, and is an objective coming in the next couple of minutes?
breaks: Wrong if nothing is spawning soon and the extra wave finishes a full item: stay, then Teleport back.
basis: pro:A late recall spends your Teleport

when: an objective spawns within a minute
asks: where do I stand before dragon
should I be with my team
how do I set up the fight
say: Get there first and wait in a brush on their path instead of standing with your team, or stay grouped if it's already swept.
more: An engage champion nobody can see makes every step toward the pit a risk. They slow down, and your team gets the area for free.
It only works for the team that arrives first; walking into their vision to hide is how supports die.
Your team must be close enough to follow the moment you go.
check: Is the brush unwarded, and is your team within range to follow your engage?
breaks: Wrong if your carries need you beside them against divers: stay with them, the hidden engage isn't worth a dead carry.
basis: pro:An unseen engager controls the approach

when: their marksman has Teleport and yours does not
asks: they keep coming back full health
how do we play this lane
why are we losing after even trades
say: Only take trades you clearly win, because he can recall and Teleport back, or match his recalls and play for your jungler.
more: An even trade leaves both sides low. He recalls, buys and Teleports back to a full wave, while you're still low or walking.
Your combat summoner only pays off if it wins a fight outright. Otherwise he is ahead by a recall each time.
Recalling when he does keeps you level and saves the fight for when a third player arrives.
check: Is his Teleport likely up, and where is the wave when he leaves?
breaks: Wrong if he already used Teleport this lane: then even trades are fine and a bad recall for him costs minions.
basis: pro:Even trades lose to a Teleport

asks: they saw us coming, still go
we got warded, do we dive
say: If you walked past a ward on the way, call it off and hold the wave, or go only if nobody else has shown yet.
more: A dive they see coming gives them time to keep the wave out of the tower and bring help. The dive needs both of those to go the other way.
Backing off costs a few seconds. Diving into a prepared lane costs kills.
The setup still counts: the wave is big, and their players moved to answer, so something else is open.
check: Did a ward see you, is the wave reaching their tower, and has anyone on their team moved toward the lane?
breaks: Wrong if the target is alone, low and nobody can arrive in time: being seen doesn't matter then.
basis: pro:A dive that was seen is a different dive

when: your team is behind after 15:00
asks: where do I ward when behind
how do we stop them invading
say: Ward the entrances to your own jungle and hold the choke points, or push a ward to river only with a wave shoved.
more: The team that's ahead wants deeper vision to find picks. Denying them your jungle entrances is the first thing a behind team can actually hold.
Wards there see them coming with time to react. A river ward placed alone usually just gets you caught.
A shoved wave is what makes the next step out safe, because someone has to answer it.
check: Which entrances have no ward, and are your lanes pushed in or out?
breaks: Wrong if an objective you must contest is about to spawn: then the river needs wards, and the whole team goes together.
basis: pro:Hold the chokes into your jungle

asks: they warded the river, how do I gank
can I get around the ward
which way do I come in
say: Come in over a wall or through the lane brush instead of the warded river, or wait for the ward to run out.
more: A gank path that skips the usual ward arrives with no warning. If your champion can cross a wall, use that entrance, not the one everyone watches.
Laners stand according to their ward. If it shows nothing, they stay far forward.
It takes a little longer to walk, so start before the wave turns around.
check: Where is their ward, can your champion cross the wall near the lane, and how far forward is the target?
breaks: Wrong if your champion has no way over terrain and the lane brush is warded too: pick a different lane.
basis: pro:Path around the ward

when: your team is behind after 20:00
asks: what do I do after pushing my wave
where do I go from side lane
how do we get a pick
do I stay in the side lane
say: Shove your side wave, then walk through your own jungle toward mid looking for someone alone, or stay if the wave comes back.
more: A pushed side wave makes one of them come and catch it. The moment after is when their team is spread between two lanes.
Moving to mid through your own jungle keeps you unseen and safe, and puts you beside your team if a pick appears.
One pick is what slows the game down and opens the next objective for a team that's behind.
check: Is the side wave pushed past the river, and who on their team is alone and visible?
breaks: Wrong if their whole team is grouped mid: there is no pick, so keep farming the side waves safely.
basis: pro:Push one lane, then look across mid
